flawed_step: Line 0678 (the Gaussian-integral evaluation inside the proof of Lemma \ref{taylor}, case c=1): "$\frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}} \int_{-\infty}^0 \exp(-(\alpha-t)^2/2)\,dt = \frac{1}{2} + \frac{1}{2}\erf(-\sqrt{2}\alpha)$". The erf argument is wrong by a factor of 2 in scale: with the definition $\erf(z)=\frac{2}{\sqrt\pi}\int_0^z e^{-t^2}dt$ given at line 0610, the correct value is $\frac12+\frac12\erf(-\alpha/\sqrt2)$. The error propagates to lines 0672, 0626 (statement of Lemma \ref{taylor}(iii)) and 0710 (Corollary (iv), the edge kernel).
counterexample: Take alpha = 1 (fixed, real; c = 1). LHS of line 0678: substitute u=(t-1)/sqrt(2), dt=sqrt(2)du; then (1/sqrt(2pi)) * int_{-inf}^{0} exp(-(1-t)^2/2) dt = (1/sqrt(pi)) * int_{-inf}^{-1/sqrt(2)} e^{-u^2} du = 1/2 + (1/2) erf(-1/sqrt(2)) = (1/2)(1 - erf(0.7071068)) = (1/2)(1 - 0.6826895) = 0.1586553. This is exactly Phi(-1), the standard normal CDF at -1, as it must be. RHS as asserted on line 0678: 1/2 + (1/2) erf(-sqrt(2)*1) = (1/2)(1 - erf(1.4142136)) = (1/2)(1 - 0.9544997) = 0.0227501. So 0.1586553 != 0.0227501; the asserted identity fails by a factor of about 7. Independent check of which side is right, directly against the object the lemma is about: put z = n + sqrt(n) (so c=1, alpha=1). Then e^{-z} sum_{j=0}^{n-1} z^j/j! = P(Poisson(z) <= n-1), and Poisson(z) has mean n+sqrt(n) and sd sqrt(n)(1+o(1)), so by the CLT this probability tends to Phi((n-1-(n+sqrt n))/sqrt n) = Phi(-1) = 0.15866, not 0.02275. (Numerically, e.g. n = 400, z = 420: P(Poisson(420) <= 399) = 0.1567, already close to 0.1587 and nowhere near 0.0228.) Hence Lemma \ref{taylor}(iii) as stated at line 0626 is false for alpha = 1, and the corrected conclusion is 1/2 + (1/2)erf(-alpha/sqrt 2) = (1/2)erfc(alpha/sqrt 2). Consistency check that the corrected form is the intended one: feeding it into Corollary (iv) at line 0710 with z_1 = z_2 = 1 gives the known complex-Ginibre edge kernel (1/pi) e^{-|w_1|^2/2-|w_2|^2/2+w_1 conj(w_2)} * (1/2) erfc((w_1 + conj(w_2))/sqrt 2), whereas the printed version yields (1/2) erfc(sqrt(2)(w_1+conj(w_2))), which is not the Ginibre edge kernel.

The false value is exactly what is asserted in the lemma statement (line 0626) and pushed into the Ginibre edge-kernel Corollary (iv) (line 0710), so it is load-bearing, not cosmetic: the corrected constant reproduces the known edge kernel (1/2)erfc((w_1+conj w_2)/sqrt 2) while the printed one does not.
